notes: Etsy is a marketplace, so per task instructions the goal was to find genuine holiday leaf nodes in Etsy's own category tree under Home & Living, not search-result pages. Tier 1 (direct HTTP): robots.txt has no Claude/Anthropic-specific disallow (checked for claude/anthropic/GPTBot/CCBot entries, found none), so proceeded. curl fetch of https://www.etsy.com/c/home-and-living returned HTTP 403 with a DataDome JS-challenge page (real bot-block, not a proxy/geo issue). WebFetch on the same URL also returned HTTP 403. Per hard-block rule, moved to the next tier rather than retrying tier 1. No standalone Playwright/CDP tool was available in this environment, so proceeded directly to Claude-in-Chrome (tier 3) as the practical next tier. The shared Chrome session is used concurrently by many other workers/tabs; had to open a dedicated new tab (tabId 1961736007) after an initial tab got hijacked mid-task by another worker's navigation. The browser's network route geo-resolved to India (etsy.com redirected to /in-en/ locale, INR currency) rather than a US IP; this only affects displayed currency/language, not the taxonomy structure or category slugs, which are global/canonical (the same /c/home-and-living/... paths and English category names apply on the US site). Navigated etsy.com/c/home-and-living, expanded 'Show more' to see all 16 top-level Home & Living subcategories: Home Decor, Furniture, Floor & Rugs, Lighting, Outdoor & Gardening, Bathroom, Kitchen & Dining, Bedding, Storage & Organisation, Curtains & Window Treatments, Spirituality & Religion, Office, Food & Drink, Home Improvement, Home Appliances, Cleaning Supplies. None is itself named 'Holiday'. Drilled into Home Decor (etsy.com/c/home-and-living/home-decor), whose own subcategory list includes 'Seasonal Decor' as a genuine taxonomy node (confirmed via breadcrumb nav and read_page href extraction, not a search page). Seasonal Decor (etsy.com/c/home-and-living/home-decor/seasonal-decor) is itself a mixed multi-holiday hub (listing shows Christmas, Halloween, Thanksgiving, Easter items together), so it was NOT recorded as its own row since rule #2 requires the site to associate a category with ONE specific holiday. However, Seasonal Decor's own direct children ARE single-holiday genuine leaf category pages, each with its own stable /c/ URL, breadcrumb trail, and H1 heading (verified via read_page href extraction, not clicking through search): Ornaments (page title 'Christmas Decorations', breadcrumb label 'Baubles') -> Christmas; Stockings (page title 'Christmas Stockings') -> Christmas; Christmas Trees -> Christmas; Tree Toppers -> Christmas; Tree Skirts -> Christmas; Easter Baskets -> Easter. All 6 of these plus the Seasonal Decor parent display 'All Filters / 1,000+ items with ads' at the top of the listing -- this is Etsy's standard capped display (it does not show an exact number once a category exceeds 1,000 items), not a search hit count. Per the qty rule (never estimate/round/infer), qty was set to null with a MANUAL REVIEW flag for every row rather than recording '1000' as if it were exact. Also spot-checked two other top-level Home & Living branches for additional holiday leaf nodes: Kitchen & Dining (subcats: Drink and Barware, Dining and Serving, Kitchen Storage, Kitchen Decor, Cookware, Linens, +3 more) and Outdoor & Garden (subcats: Garden Decoration, Patio Furniture, Planters and Pots, Plants, Mailboxes, Seeds and Seed Bombs, +14 more) -- neither exposed a holiday-named leaf category in its visible subcategory list, so no additional rows were added from those branches. No Diwali, Valentine's Day, Thanksgiving, Halloween, or New Year leaf category nodes were found anywhere in the browsed taxonomy (those holidays only appear as product listings mixed inside the generic Seasonal Decor hub, which is excluded per the search/mixed-category exclusion rule). Search-results pages (e.g. /search?q=christmas) were not used for any row per the task's explicit exclusion of search as a category.
